title: Apache Spark vs VecRuntime vs DataFusion Comet on TPC-DS 1 TB
dataset: TPC-DS scale factor 1000 (1 TB), Parquet on Amazon S3 (103 query variants, one measured iteration each, no warm-up)
cluster: Amazon EKS 1.36; 9 x m5.4xlarge (16 vCPU, 64 GB, x86-64 with AVX-512), 300 GB root volume; one node group in one availability zone (us-east-1a), the driver on the ninth node
executors: 8 executors x 13 cores x 50 GB each (Spark: 20 GB heap / 30 GB overhead; VecRuntime: 30 GB heap / 20 GB overhead; Comet: 20 GB heap / 8 GB overhead / 22 GB off-heap; Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime: 30 GB heap / 12 GB overhead / 8 GB off-heap); driver 2 cores x 4 GB
storage: Amazon S3 through an S3 gateway VPC endpoint, Hadoop 3.4.3 S3A with the Analytics Accelerator input stream (the default in 3.4.3); fs.s3a.connection.maximum=1000, threads.max=256, max.total.tasks=128, Analytics Accelerator physicalio.thread.pool.size=192 for every engine (#566)

versions.JDK: Amazon Corretto 25, -XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders and Amazon Corretto Crypto Provider on driver and executors (#578, #566)
versions.VecRuntime: main at 77283b2 (native Parquet scan on by default #609, reduce-side locality off #604, scan locality #607)

common_conf: spark.locality.wait=0   # every engine (#608): no locality wait; on S3 the scans have no locality, and Spark's reduce-side preference piled post-shuffle stages onto one host
# spark.sql.adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes left at Spark's default (64 MB); no coalescePartitions.minPartitionNum
vector_conf: spark.vecruntime.scan.nativeParquet.enabled=true   # our Parquet reader, VectorParquetScanExec (#559); the default since #609
spark.vecruntime.shuffle.reduceLocality.enabled=false   # default (#604): our reduce tasks report no preferred locations
spark.vecruntime.scan.nativeParquet.prefetchFiles=6   # default: files read ahead per split
spark.vecruntime.scan.nativeParquet.prefetchRowGroups=2   # default: row groups read ahead per file
spark.vecruntime.shuffle.aqe.mapSizeScaling=true   # AQE sees Spark-scale map output sizes (#514)
mixed_conf: spark.comet.scan.enabled=true   # CometNativeScanExec: DataFusion's Rust Parquet reader and object_store S3 I/O
spark.comet.exec.enabled=true   # with every Comet operator switched off: filter, project, aggregate, joins, sort, window, ...
spark.memory.offHeap.size=8g   # executors 30 GB heap / 12 GB overhead / 8 GB off-heap
notes: Every engine returned Spark's row counts on every query, and Spark's checksums on every query except q65, whose result has ties that every engine orders differently.

The four legs ran on 2026-10-03 in one cluster session on the same nine nodes, one after another (Spark, VecRuntime, Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime, Comet), each alone on the cluster. S3 throughput varies between sessions, so only legs from one session are compared.

VecRuntime runs on its own Parquet reader (spark.vecruntime.scan.nativeParquet.enabled, #559), the default since #609: pages decoded in Java straight into the Arrow buffers its operators read, with the next files and row groups of each split read ahead on background threads.

Every engine ran with spark.locality.wait=0 (#608). Against the 2026-10-02 run, which kept Spark's 3 s wait, Spark went from 3,099 to 2,963 s, VecRuntime from 1,542 to 1,415 s (with #604 as well), Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime from 1,954 to 1,813 s and Comet from 1,999 to 1,964 s.
Comet is the 1.0.0 release from Maven Central. The S3A settings, ACCP and compact object headers are the benchmark launcher's defaults since #566 and #578 and apply to all four engines.
AQE is at its defaults for every engine.
methodology_html: Methodology. Spark, VecRuntime, Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime and Comet ran one after another in one cluster session on 2026-10-03, on the same nine nodes, each alone on the cluster, over the same S3 data with the same Spark settings; only the execution engine and its own memory split differ (every engine has 50 GB per executor; where it puts them follows where it allocates). Each query ran once after the plan was compiled; the time is the wall-clock of the query's execution as the runner measures it.
wins_html: The scan-bound queries are VecRuntime's, on its own Parquet reader: q88 35.1 s against Spark's 94.3 and Comet's 83.0; q9 32.0 against 76.9 and 52.0; q28 60.7 against 97.4 and 69.2; q44 10.2 against 34.1 and 24.1; q90 9.6 against 27.2 and 27.8. So are the heavy joins: q23b 91.9 against 273.6 and 133.2; q64 24.5 against 88.5 and 54.7; q93 41.6 against 129.4 and 76.9. Comet Native Scan + VecRuntime (the same operators on Comet's Rust reader) finishes in 1,813 s against VecRuntime's 1,415 s on its own reader. Comet leads on q95 (27 s ahead), the heavy aggregates (q4 51.4 against VecRuntime's 62.1, q11 29.2 against 33.6), q65, q51, q96 and q18. VecRuntime's losses to Spark are q99 (9.0 s against 8.4, the join-chain gather of #603), q96 (15.5 against 14.6) and q12 (2.3 against 2.1).
vector_vs_comet: and leads on the scan-bound queries and the heavy joins; Comet leads on q95, the heavy aggregates (q4, q11) and q18
results_line: Every engine returned Spark's results (q65: ties, ordered differently by every engine).
mixed_line: Same operators and shuffle as VecRuntime, on Comet's Rust Parquet reader.
